requirements_summary: Workload: conversational support + product search reranking during peak shopping windows.
Target concurrency: 400-600 active sessions, peak bursts to 1,200 concurrent short requests.
Throughput requirement: sustained ~18k tokens/s; peak burst up to 40k tokens/s for 30-minute sale events.
Latency SLOs requested (client expectation): p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 450ms for non-streaming short-turn requests (<=128 tokens).
Streaming expectations: first-byte p95 <= 150ms, full-stream completion depends on token count but client needs predictable per-token latency for throttling.
Fallback model routing: require automatic downgrade to 7B quantized variant with routing policy and explicit developer-visible fallback metrics.
Data residency: EU users must route to eu-region Dedicated pool for PCI-adjacent data.
Security: SSO (SAML), enterprise KMS, audit logs shipped to client's Splunk cluster, retention controls for PII tokens.
poc_notes: POC target: 4-week pilot, canary to 5% of traffic after week 1, ramp to 25% by week 3.
Infra: reserved 8xA100 equivalent pool; autoscale headroom to add 4xA100 burst nodes for flash sales (billing trap defined).
Evaluation metrics: end-to-end client-side latency (browser/edge) vs server-side processing time; Redwood console token-level cost breakdown; error rate; fallback events.
Instrumentation: require synchronous timestamps and trace-id propagation. Client will run synthetic load from 3 regions (us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1) using Locust + internal RUM agent.

Measurement alignment ask: Redwood to provide definition doc mapping Redwood server-side metrics to client-side measurements (how queuing, TLS handshake, TCP connect, and edge-router time are counted).
Client quote: "We need the SLO to reflect what our customers feel — not just the kernel exec time." — Head of Platform (J. Alvarez).
negotiation_notes: Legal request: explicit mean-time-to-recover (MTTR) for model failover and region-to-region fallback, incl. compensation bands.
SLA metric granularity: client insists on p99 measured at ingress client-side (edge) for public-facing latency guarantees; Redwood proposes server-side p99 with agreed correction factors.
Measurement reconciliation plan: weekly alignment calls during pilot, shared Prometheus queries + sample traces for disputed periods.
Pricing: baseline reserved capacity + per-token for burst overage; client wants a cap on monthly burst charges during Black Friday equivalent window.
